summary: Hari Shankar Prasad is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University under Ramakant Tripathi and doctoral supervisor Jan Willem de Jong.

Haridas Bhattacharyya (1891–1956) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, the University of Dhaka, and Banaras Hindu University.
Haridas Sinharay was an Indologist who held a post at Maulana Azad College, attested in 1970 and 1990.

Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani (1917–2001) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Samaldas Arts College and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan under Muni Jinavijaya, he held posts at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Gujarat University, and the L. D. Institute of Indology.

Harjot Oberoi is a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University, and held a chair at the University of British Columbia from around 1987.
Harogadde Manappa Nayak (1931–2000) was a linguist who served as Director at the University of Mysore (circa 1967–1984) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold C. Conklin (1926–2016) was a linguist who earned his bachelor's from UC Berkeley and his Ph.D. from Yale. He taught at Columbia and Yale University, where he also served as Curator of Anthropology at the Peabody Museum.

Harold G. Coward is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. from McMaster University in 1973. He held posts as professor at the University of Calgary and director at the University of Victoria.

Harold Hargreaves (1876–1951) was an Indologist and archaeologist who served as headmaster at Government High School, Amritsar, and later worked for the Archaeological Survey of India as Superintendent and Deputy Director General.

Harold Scheub (1931–2019) studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he earned his PhD. He taught at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School before his long tenure at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Harold Stewart (1916–1995) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Harold Walter Bailey (1899–1996) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguist. Educated at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under Frederick William Thomas, he taught Iranian studies at SOAS and held the Sanskrit chair at Cambridge.

Haroon Khan Sherwani (1891–1980) was a historian and Indologist. Educated at Aligarh Muslim University and the University of Oxford, and mentored by Ghulam Yazdani, he held posts at Osmania University, Nizam College, and Zakir Husain Delhi College.

Harry Falk is an Indologist and linguist who held a post at the University of Freiburg from around 1979 to 1993, and later served as Professor of Indology and Director at the Free University of Berlin from 1993 to 2012.

Hartmut Buescher is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhāl Tripathi, later holding posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.
Hartmut Scharfe (1932–2020) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Paul Thieme for his doctorate and held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel is an Indologist who served in the Prussian State Library's Oriental Department, headed the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland, and led a project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Nagasaki University from around 1976 to 2004.
Haruka Yanagisawa (1944–2015) was a scholar of Indology and history who held academic posts at Chiba University (circa 1978–1992) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1992–2007).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed an MA and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, where Robert E. Buswell Jr. served as doctoral supervisor.
